description: Change the starting cargo capacity to 10.
steps: Find the player/ship initial state or balance configuration that controls starting cargo capacity.
Set the starting cargo capacity to 10 without changing cargo upgrade increments unless required by tests or gameplay consistency.
Update HUD/default labels or persistence/reset behavior if they assume the old starting capacity.
acceptance: A new game starts with cargo capacity 10.
The cargo HUD displays 0/10 at game start.
Existing cargo upgrades and saved-game reset behavior still work correctly.
The full test/build command passes.

description: Make low fuel and low hull/health HUD bars flash to draw attention.
steps: Find the HUD rendering code for the fuel and hull/health bars.
Define clear low/critical thresholds for fuel and hull/health, reusing existing warning thresholds if they already exist.
Add a visible flashing/pulsing effect around the fuel bar when fuel is low.
Add a visible flashing/pulsing effect around the hull/health bar when hull/health is low.
Keep the effect readable and not overwhelming during normal play.
acceptance: The fuel bar visibly flashes or pulses when fuel is below the chosen low-fuel threshold.
The hull/health bar visibly flashes or pulses when hull/health is below the chosen low-health threshold.
The bars do not flash while their values are safely above the thresholds.
The effect works during gameplay and after save/load or reset paths that update HUD state.
The full test/build command passes.

description: Make the cargo bar flash when cargo is full.
steps: Find the HUD rendering code for the cargo bar and cargo capacity state.
Detect when current cargo is at or above cargo capacity.
Add a visible flashing/pulsing effect around the cargo bar while cargo is full.
Ensure the effect stops immediately once cargo is sold, deposited, or otherwise reduced below capacity.
acceptance: The cargo bar visibly flashes or pulses when cargo is full.
The cargo bar does not flash when cargo is below capacity.
The effect updates correctly after mining, selling/depositing cargo, upgrades, save/load, and reset flows.
The full test/build command passes.

description: Migrate the current HTML-based GUI to React.
steps: Inspect the existing index.html and JavaScript UI/HUD code to identify static markup, dynamic HUD updates, controls, overlays, and game canvas mounting behavior.
Add React and React DOM to the Vite project and introduce a React entry point without breaking the game loop or canvas rendering.
Move the GUI/HUD markup currently defined in HTML into React components, keeping IDs/classes/data hooks or replacing them with equivalent integration points for existing game logic.
Refactor DOM update code as needed so React owns the GUI while gameplay systems can still update HUD state predictably.
Preserve existing visuals, controls, save/load/reset behavior, and responsive layout during the migration.
Add or update tests around GUI state/rendering boundaries where practical.
acceptance: The game runs with the GUI rendered by React components instead of static HTML markup.
Existing HUD values, flashing alerts, controls, overlays, and canvas/gameplay interactions continue to work after migration.
index.html is reduced to the Vite root/container markup and script entry point rather than containing the full GUI.
The full test/build command passes.

description: Migrate the codebase from JavaScript to TypeScript.
steps: Inspect the existing JavaScript files, Vite configuration, tests, and module boundaries to plan an incremental TypeScript migration.
Add TypeScript tooling and configuration to the Vite project, including appropriate tsconfig settings and npm scripts if needed.
Rename source and test files from .js/.jsx to .ts/.tsx where appropriate, adding explicit types for shared game state, systems, HUD integration, and persistence data.
Resolve type errors without weakening checks unnecessarily, using clear interfaces/types for core game objects and DOM integration points.
Keep runtime behavior, save/load compatibility, tests, and build output unchanged except for the TypeScript migration.
acceptance: The project source and tests build and run through TypeScript-aware tooling.
Core gameplay state, HUD/UI integration, persistence, and utility modules have meaningful TypeScript types instead of broad any-style placeholders where practical.
Existing gameplay, controls, save/load/reset behavior, HUD flashing alerts, and React GUI migration compatibility are preserved.
The full test/build command passes.
